mastery_target: Explain how cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems are organized.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows levels of organization in the human body from simplest to most complex?

answer_choices.A: organ system → organ → tissue → cell
answer_choices.B: cell → tissue → organ → organ system
answer_choices.C: tissue → cell → organ system → organ
answer_choices.D: organ → cell → tissue → organ system

questions.explanation: Cells are the basic units of living things. Similar cells work together as tissues, tissues work together as organs, and organs work together as organ systems.

questions.prompt: What is a tissue?

answer_choices.A: A group of similar cells working together
answer_choices.B: A group of organs working together
answer_choices.C: A single body system
answer_choices.D: A part of a cell that performs one job

questions.explanation: A tissue is made of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes an organ?

answer_choices.A: A group of tissues working together to perform a function
answer_choices.B: A group of identical cells with no specific function
answer_choices.C: A single cell that controls the whole body
answer_choices.D: A group of organ systems working together

questions.explanation: An organ is made of different tissues that work together to do a job for the body.

questions.prompt: Which example shows organs working together as an organ system?

answer_choices.A: Muscle cells forming muscle tissue
answer_choices.B: Nerve cells forming nervous tissue
answer_choices.C: The stomach and intestines working together in digestion
answer_choices.D: Skin cells forming skin tissue

questions.explanation: The stomach and intestines are organs. When organs work together for a major body function, they form an organ system.

questions.prompt: Which level of organization is made directly from cells?

answer_choices.A: Tissue
answer_choices.B: Organ
answer_choices.C: Organ system
answer_choices.D: Whole organism

questions.explanation: Cells with similar structures and functions can work together to form tissues.

questions.prompt: Which level of organization includes the heart, blood vessels, and blood working together?

answer_choices.A: Cell
answer_choices.B: Tissue
answer_choices.C: Organ
answer_choices.D: Organ system

questions.explanation: The heart, blood vessels, and blood work together as parts of the circulatory system, which is an organ system.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows a muscle cell, muscle tissue, a muscle, and the muscular system. What idea does the diagram best show?

answer_choices.A: Body structures are organized from cells into larger systems
answer_choices.B: All organs have the same type of tissue
answer_choices.C: Cells are larger than organ systems
answer_choices.D: Organ systems are not made of organs

questions.explanation: The diagram shows the biological organization pattern: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form organ systems.

questions.prompt: A student is sorting body structures into levels of organization. Which item should be placed in the tissue category?

answer_choices.A: A red blood cell
answer_choices.B: Cardiac muscle tissue
answer_choices.C: The heart
answer_choices.D: The circulatory system

questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle tissue is made of similar muscle cells working together. The heart is an organ, and the circulatory system is an organ system.

questions.prompt: A model shows epithelial tissue, muscle tissue, nervous tissue, and connective tissue all working together in the stomach. What level of organization is the stomach?

answer_choices.A: Cell
answer_choices.B: Tissue
answer_choices.C: Organ
answer_choices.D: Organ system

questions.explanation: The stomach is an organ because it contains multiple tissues that work together to perform a function.

questions.prompt: A student claims that the lungs are an organ system because they help the body breathe. Which correction is most accurate?

answer_choices.A: The lungs are organs; they are part of the respiratory system.
answer_choices.B: The lungs are tissues; they are made of organ systems.
answer_choices.C: The lungs are cells; they combine to make tissue.
answer_choices.D: The lungs are not part of any level of organization.

questions.explanation: The lungs are organs. They work with other structures, such as the trachea and diaphragm, as part of the respiratory system.

questions.prompt: Which example correctly matches a body structure to its level of organization?

answer_choices.A: Neuron — organ system
answer_choices.B: Nervous tissue — tissue
answer_choices.C: Brain — cell
answer_choices.D: Nervous system — organ

questions.explanation: Nervous tissue is a tissue because it is made of cells that work together. A neuron is a cell, the brain is an organ, and the nervous system is an organ system.

questions.prompt: A chart lists these structures: skin cell, skin tissue, skin, integumentary system. Which structure is an organ?

answer_choices.A: Skin cell
answer_choices.B: Skin tissue
answer_choices.C: Skin
answer_choices.D: Integumentary system

questions.explanation: Skin is an organ because it is made of multiple tissues working together. The integumentary system is an organ system.

questions.prompt: In BODY_MODEL_01, the labels show cell → tissue → organ → organ system. If the tissue label were removed, which structure would most likely belong in that missing position?

answer_choices.A: A single muscle cell
answer_choices.B: A group of muscle cells working together
answer_choices.C: A whole muscle
answer_choices.D: The muscular system

questions.explanation: A tissue is made of a group of similar cells working together. A whole muscle is an organ, and the muscular system is an organ system.

questions.prompt: Which statement uses evidence from levels of organization to explain why the heart is an organ?

answer_choices.A: The heart is an organ because it is located inside the body.
answer_choices.B: The heart is an organ because different tissues in it work together to pump blood.
answer_choices.C: The heart is an organ because it is smaller than a cell.
answer_choices.D: The heart is an organ because it works alone without other body parts.

questions.explanation: This statement uses evidence: the heart contains different tissues that work together for a function. That is what makes it an organ.

questions.prompt: A student argues, “A tissue and an organ are the same thing because both are made of cells.” Which response best explains the error?

answer_choices.A: The student is correct because every body part is one level of organization.
answer_choices.B: The student is incorrect because tissues are made of similar cells, while organs are made of multiple tissues working together.
answer_choices.C: The student is incorrect because tissues are larger than organ systems.
answer_choices.D: The student is correct because organs cannot contain tissues.

questions.explanation: Both tissues and organs contain cells, but they are different levels. Tissues are groups of similar cells, while organs are made of multiple tissues working together.

questions.prompt: A model shows many similar muscle cells arranged together. The model then shows those groups combining with other tissues to form a whole muscle. Which conclusion is best supported?

answer_choices.A: Cells can combine to form tissues, and tissues can combine to form organs.
answer_choices.B: Organ systems combine to form cells.
answer_choices.C: A tissue is always more complex than an organ.
answer_choices.D: All organs are made of only one type of cell.

questions.explanation: The model supports the conclusion that body organization builds from cells to tissues and from tissues to organs.

questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported by the evidence that the digestive system includes the mouth, esophagus, stomach, and intestines?

answer_choices.A: The digestive system is a tissue because it contains similar cells.
answer_choices.B: The digestive system is an organ system because multiple organs work together.
answer_choices.C: The digestive system is a cell because it performs one function.
answer_choices.D: The digestive system is an organ because it is made of only one tissue.

questions.explanation: The evidence lists several organs working together. That supports the claim that the digestive system is an organ system.

questions.prompt: In BODY_MODEL_02, the stomach is shown containing several tissue layers and also connected to other digestive organs. Which explanation best uses the model?

answer_choices.A: The stomach is a tissue because it has layers.
answer_choices.B: The stomach is an organ made of tissues and is part of an organ system with other organs.
answer_choices.C: The stomach is an organ system because it contains cells.
answer_choices.D: The stomach is a cell because it has a specific function.

questions.explanation: The model gives two pieces of evidence: the stomach contains tissues, making it an organ, and it connects with other organs in an organ system.

questions.prompt: A student says, “The brain and spinal cord are both organs, so together they are still just one organ.” Which evidence best challenges this idea?

answer_choices.A: Organs that work together for a major function form an organ system.
answer_choices.B: Organs are always smaller than tissues.
answer_choices.C: Cells cannot be part of tissues.
answer_choices.D: A body system must contain only one organ.

questions.explanation: When organs such as the brain and spinal cord work together for a major function, they are part of an organ system.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects all four levels of organization?

answer_choices.A: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form organ systems.
answer_choices.B: Organ systems form organs, organs form cells, and cells form tissues.
answer_choices.C: Tissues form cells, cells form organ systems, and organ systems form organs.
answer_choices.D: Organs form tissues, tissues form organ systems, and organ systems form cells.

questions.explanation: The correct organization pattern is cell to tissue to organ to organ system. Each level is made from parts of the level before it.

questions.prompt: A model shows this evidence: individual cells are grouped into tissue, several tissues are grouped into an organ, and several organs are grouped into a body system. Which claim is best supported by the model?

answer_choices.A: The body is organized in levels that increase in complexity.
answer_choices.B: Cells and organ systems are the same level of organization.
answer_choices.C: Tissues are made of organ systems.
answer_choices.D: Organs do not contain cells.

questions.explanation: The model supports the claim that body organization increases in complexity from cells to tissues to organs to organ systems.
